title: USWNT to play Panama in Southern California friendly in January 2027
content:
The U.S. women’s national team will begin their 2027 campaign with a return to Southern California for a friendly against Panama, the federation announced today.

On Jan. 12, the USWNT will face off against the Central American nation at Dignity Health Sports Park in Carson, Calif., in the first fixture between the two teams outside of a Concacaf competition. The U.S. have won each of the three games they have played against Panama.

“January camp gives us the chance to hit the ground running in 2027 and perhaps see some younger players before the SheBelieves Cup at the end of February,” said USWNT head coach Emma Hayes in a press release.

The January match will take place after the Concacaf W Championship later this month. The regional tournament held in Mansfield, Texas, serves as qualification for the 2027 World Cup in Brazil as well as the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles, for which the U.S. have already qualified for as hosts.

Both the U.S. and Panama have reached the Concacaf W Championship quarterfinals, which begin on Nov. 27. The four teams to advance from the quarterfinals will automatically qualify for the World Cup, while the remaining four will compete against each other for an additional two spots. Those two teams will be entered in the interconfederational playoffs, which commence in February.

El Salvador will play the USWNT in those Concacaf quarterfinals on Nov. 27, while Canada meet Panama on Nov. 28.

Dignity Health Sports Park is familiar territory for the USWNT, having played there more than any other venue in the country and possessing an all-time record of 20-1-1 at the stadium.

Panama were World Cup debutants in 2023. Las Canaleras did not advance from their group, a tough task against Brazil, Jamaica, and France, but their first goal in tournament history, scored by midfielder Marta Cox from a long range free kick, was among one of the World Cup’s unforgettable moments.

The USWNT, meanwhile, will be looking to firm up its roster for the World Cup, particularly in light of injuries or prolonged absences of key players this year. They have qualified for every edition of the tournament and won a record four times, but have a lot to prove in 2027, should they qualify, after their worst-ever finish in program history in 2023 when they were knocked out of the round of 16 by Sweden on penalties.

“We know the players will be coming off their holiday break, but we cherish every training session we get together so we’re looking forward to having a great training environment in Southern California to kick off the year,” Hayes said.

The USWNT roster for the Concacaf W Championship hasn’t yet been released but is expected to be announced this week.
